name: study-3-adaptive-chemotaxis
title: Study 3 — adaptive chemotaxis: move toward food to survive
objective:
Place the precarious individual in an environment with a nutrient gradient and give
it a sensorimotor loop: sense the local nutrient, run-and-tumble (tumble less when
nutrient is rising), move. The nutrient feeds the metabolism that maintains the
membrane that keeps it alive. Show that a chemotactic agent climbs the gradient,
finds food, and survives — while a blind agent random-walks, starves, and dissolves.
This is where life becomes mind: the gradient is MEANINGFUL from the perspective of
the precarious identity (up-gradient = viable, down-gradient = dissolution). Value is
grounded in the cell's own viability, not assigned from outside — sense-making, and
agency in service of self-maintenance.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
A chemotactic agent out-survives a blind one by finding and staying at food;
without sensing, the agent cannot maintain viability and dissolves.

behavior_tests.name: chemotaxis-survival
behavior_tests.description:
Agents that sense the gradient and move up it survive: the chemotactic
population maintains viability by finding and staying at food.

behavior_tests.name: agency-advantage
behavior_tests.description:
Agency is in service of survival: chemotactic agents out-survive blind ones
(survival_advantage = chemotactic_survival / blind_survival). Disable sensing
and the agent dissolves — the sensorimotor loop is constitutive of staying alive.

provenance.note: 1.5x advantage band set so sensing must clearly beat the blind random-walk control (~0.35 survival); calibrated against the negative control rather than a literature effect size (observed 2.33x ± 0.26 over 12 seeds).

behavior_tests.name: sense-making
behavior_tests.description:
The gradient is meaningful to a self with something at stake: chemotactic agents
experience more food than blind ones (gradient_advantage) — they make the
environment matter from the perspective of their own viability.

provenance.note: >1 means the agent experiences more food than chance; 1.15 is a minimal "the gradient is made to matter" margin above parity — a theory-motivated floor for sense-making, not a calibrated or literature value.

findings.statement: Agency in service of survival: chemotactic agents climb the gradient, find food, and survive (79%), while blind agents random-walk and dissolve (only 35% survive) — a 2.3× survival advantage (mean ± 0.26 across 12 seeds; 12/12 favour sensing). Without sensing, the agent cannot maintain viability.
findings.next_action: Add a weakly-sensing (borderline) agent so the survival metric is calibrated across fail→borderline→pass, not just the pass/fail extremes (review C4).

findings.statement: Sense-making: the nutrient gradient is meaningful from the perspective of the precarious identity — chemotactic agents experience 1.39× more food than blind ones. Value (food = viable) is grounded in the cell's own viability, not assigned from outside. (Interpretation: 'sense-making' is the autopoietic reading of an engineered sensing→tumble response, not a claim of cognition.)

controls.name: chemotactic-agent
controls.hypothesis: A sensing agent in a gradient should survive (the qualifying, autopoietic-agency end).

controls.name: blind-motile-agent
controls.hypothesis: A motile-but-non-sensing agent (random walk, no gradient sensing) should survive markedly worse if sensing — not mere movement — drives survival.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The survival gain is plain movement toward resources, not gradient sensing / sense-making.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: the blind-motile-agent control (moves by random walk but does not sense the gradient) survives far worse, so movement alone does not account for the gain.

falsifiability: The survival advantage — and the agency / sense-making reading — would be unsupported if the motile-but-blind control matched chemotactic survival, i.e. if the gain were due to movement alone rather than gradient sensing.
limitations: Demonstrates that gradient sensing improves survival and excludes the 'mere movement' explanation (blind-motile control); it does NOT establish cognition or strong agency beyond adaptive behaviour, the sensing->tumble response is an engineered rule (not emergent), and the result rests on a single run (no seed replication).

resolved_uncertainties: Gradient sensing yields a robust survival advantage (2.33x +/- 0.26 over 12 seeds; 12/12 favour sensing).
The blind-motile control excludes 'mere movement': a motile agent that cannot sense survives far worse.
remaining_uncertainties: No positive/borderline calibration case (e.g. a weakly-sensing agent) to calibrate the survival metric across its range.
'Agency' and 'sense-making' remain an autopoietic INTERPRETATION of an engineered sensing->tumble rule, not demonstrated cognition.

alternate_hypotheses.hypothesis: The gain comes from spatial resource concentration, not directed sensing.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: food is localised; even undirected agents starting near it could survive better.
discriminating_observables: survival under a uniform-resource control (no gradient) vs the localised gradient
survival of a weakly-sensing agent (borderline calibration case)

followup_study_proposals.title: Weakly-sensing agent (calibration case)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: A positive/borderline control to calibrate the survival metric across fail->borderline->pass (review C4).

followup_study_proposals.title: Parasitic / dependent agent
followup_study_proposals.motivation: An agent that exploits others' uptake blurs self-production vs dependence — stress-tests the framework (review C12).

derived.insight: Agency in service of survival: chemotactic agents climb the gradient, find food, and survive (79%), while blind agents random-walk and dissolve (only 35% survive) — a 2.3× survival advantage (mean ± 0.26 across 12 seeds; 12/12 favour sensing). Without sensing, the agent cannot maintain viability.
